title: Design System: Open Neo RTS native menus and match HUD

replayAnalytics.world: Scoped Graphite Command Stations extension: existing square graphite frames, warm-metal actions/selected wells, ivory synchronized focus, compact Arial and original queued-unit thumbnails. No new tokens, identity or artwork.
replayAnalytics.layout: G and the original graph pictogram toggle an optional nonmodal pane below player observations, above transport and beside the usable battlefield/map. Four equal tabs precede the chart metric choice or scrolling Production/Orders body. Bounded height uses remaining viewport space; original queue thumbnails wrap to available width.
replayAnalytics.charts: Economy and Military draw copied resource/inventory history directly through Babylon GUI Canvas, with Force legends, alternating line patterns and complete semantic sampled-value tables. Shared post-match income math excludes opening stock and refunds; army recruitment costs remain separate by resource.
replayAnalytics.production: Original queued-unit thumbnails group by producer, draw actual progress and expose name, work state and percentage through contextual help. All queues remain reachable through pointer and keyboard scrolling.
replayAnalytics.orders: Accepted-order APM precedes totals and active time; human and bot controllers are identified separately. Selection, camera and refused inputs never count as orders.
replayAnalytics.semantics: Semantic tabs, metric selects and table/queue regions retain keyboard ownership and mirror native focus. Tab arrows and scrolling arrows, Page Up/Down and Home/End remain usable; actual loading/empty states stay visible.
replayAnalytics.boundary: Only a verified settled terminal-replay host publishes opted-in details under existing per-seat permissions. Closing opts out; seek/vision changes discard stale analysis. Ordinary live-seat detailed statistics remain final-only; canonical history, hashes and simulation version are unchanged.
replayAnalytics.qualification: Corrected-font replay/paid-production browser journeys passed all four cases in current stable Google Chrome and current Playwright WebKit at desktop/narrow widths. Twelve actual captures are recorded under .impeccable/review/; cached-font and Canvas-text probes passed 1440-to-390-to-1440 resizing in both browsers. Earlier passing captures with cached font sizing are superseded. Final finish review is separate. No detector rerun; inherited force-opponent advisory remains advisory. Recorded cameras are documented separately in extensions.replayCameras. Delayed live spectating, full-phase acceptance, physical touch/IME, screen readers, maximum-size replay stress and hardware FPS remain open.

deviceAudio.world: Local extension of Graphite Command Stations: incumbent square graphite fields, ivory labels, warm-metal actions and coral alerts; no new tokens, palette, artwork or motion.
deviceAudio.ownership: One app-owned Babylon Audio V2 mixer survives navigation and activates lazily through a user gesture. Master plus Music, Effects, Unit voices, Announcer, Interface and Ambience levels remain presentation-side; screens own disposable playback scopes.
deviceAudio.editor: Settings from Home and a match open the same native Audio pane. Channel and integer 0–100% choices preview immediately. Test sound uses the selected channel, with Master testing Interface. Mute all and mute when unfocused preserve channel levels; Defaults previews provisional defaults.
deviceAudio.persistence: Apply saves a separate versioned device profile. Back/cancel restores saved levels. Failed writes preserve both the saved profile and editable preview, with visible recovery.
deviceAudio.help: Only Audio marks title-derived descriptions as contextual native hover/focus tooltips and hidden semantic aria-describedby text. Status and errors remain visible; incumbent permanent help outside Audio remains unchanged.
deviceAudio.layout: Back/title stay in the fixed header; responsive body content and actions scroll. Shared native dropdowns clamp to the viewport and contain an inner ScrollViewer, initially revealing the selected value. Wheel, scrollbar drag and pointer selection reach all 101 percentages and long Controls action lists.
deviceAudio.scope: Original first-playable effects and menu/match music are implemented. Announcer speech/subtitles/queue, other-roster clips, full-mix qualification and replay audio remain open; this does not complete first-playable audio.
deviceAudio.qualification: Implementation evidence does not qualify hardware hearing, OS media keys, physical touch/IME, screen readers, Firefox or hardware FPS.
deviceAudio.music: Original menu and in-match tracks use committed scene ownership, presentation-only shuffle, Music/Master levels, mute/focus handling and announcer-bus ducking. Speech and queue/subtitles remain unfinished. See ../../docs/project/decisions/2026-11-05-first-playable-music.md.

matchInputBindings.scope: Versioned device-local profile for currently implemented normal-match keyboard actions; debug/replay shortcuts, mouse/audio options and unimplemented actions retain their own scope.
matchInputBindings.editor: Shared native panel with category/action and primary/alternate choices, up to two physical key-code chords or no binding. Capture, Clear, per-action defaults and Grid/WASD presets stage changes until Apply. Escape or window blur cancels capture. Conflicts name actions and block Apply; capture and asynchronous import disable competing controls.
matchInputBindings.portability: Bounded JSON import validates into the staged profile; Export downloads the staged profile. Apply persists before refreshing the active match and live captions; persistence failure keeps the previous profile.
matchInputBindings.grid: Stable command slots use QWER/ASDF/ZXCV defaults independently of the live key captions. B and I are editable Build/train and Details defaults.
matchInputBindings.wasd: Provisional F1-free preset: W/A/S/D camera pan; numeric command slots; Alt-number group select, Ctrl+Alt-number set and Alt+Shift-number add; bracket speed controls with numpad alternatives.
matchInputBindings.qualification: Physical-key and OS accelerator capture remain unqualified.

breakpoints.name: panel-two-columns
breakpoints.value: inner content width >= 650px × effective panel scale

breakpoints.name: gallery-two-columns
breakpoints.value: inner content width >= 760px × effective panel scale

breakpoints.name: replay-compact
breakpoints.value: viewport width < 700px; map 112px rather than 204px, multiplied by min(device UI scale, max(0.8, viewport width / 420))

breakpoints.name: content-tools-stacked
breakpoints.value: viewport width <= 760px; model 42dvh above the 58dvh controls pane

home-body.purpose: Arial supporting introduction; base size multiplied by bounded device UI scale.

home-action.purpose: Native GUI action labels; the wordmark is vector paths rather than a font.

home-support.purpose: Local-match preview note; version and secondary controls use 12px base.

setup-heading.purpose: Forces, Map and Rules headings retain their base font size while surrounding geometry scales.

setup-body.purpose: Starting-kit note, map description, fixed rules and feedback.

setup-field.purpose: Native numeric text controls; semantic and native edits share the validator.

setup-action.purpose: Native framed actions and narrow faction labels.

panel-title.purpose: Bold 27px base; inherits Babylon’s current default Arial family. Multiplied by the effective panel scale.

panel-body.purpose: Explicit Arial for paragraph/caption TextBlocks; 15px base, shared by action sizes. Paragraph reservation uses measured wraps at 1.4 times font size per line.

panel-field.purpose: 16px base native input/choice text; family inherits Babylon’s current default. Native editors survive save-list updates; semantic keyboard editing mirrors focus, caret and selection while HTML retains keyboard and clipboard ownership.

panel-help.purpose: Explicit Arial help at 13px base; status/errors share that size with inherited family. Empty supporting blocks reserve no extra height.

body.purpose: Explicit Arial for native action descriptions, Details, command mode and feedback; measured wrapping at 1.4 times font size.

title.purpose: Bold Arial actor name/count at 13px base, multiplied by effective match scale; Force ownership uses a supporting 11px scaled label.

label.purpose: Explicit Arial for resource values, health and text-only action names.

hotkey.purpose: Compact fixed-size corner hint; not a minimum size for explanatory text.

motion.name: home-model-rotation
motion.purpose: Slow authored-model display rotation; disabled by either device or OS reduced-motion preference.

motion.name: harvester-work
motion.value: Authored harvest loop on the presentation clock; unload pose sampled from actual completed dock ticks.
motion.purpose: Communicate projected Supply Truck mining and unloading, preserving pause, suspended work and rest reset.

fieldManual.world: Incumbent Graphite Command Stations extension: square graphite panels, warm-metal actions/selected wells, ivory synchronized focus, existing rich Arial tables and original actor icons. No new palette, type system or shipping rasters.
fieldManual.scope: 15 actor entries: the 14-entry Eastern Collective roster plus neutral Resource Extractor, with four guide entries for economy, fog, combat and current keyboard bindings (19 entries total). All entries, Units, Structures and Concepts and controls filters accompany search, including guide titles and text. Installed compiled statistics, costs, requirements, weapon facts and expandable armour multipliers retain target/final-damage caveats; Produces/Builds relationships are filtered to the current roster.
fieldManual.entry: /manual, Home and the paused-match menu share the same browsing controller. Embedded browsing and isolated model inspection preserve the paused world.
fieldManual.layout: Shared 1240px scaled gallery cap and 760px scaled inner-width threshold. Manual alone uses 32% roster and 68% detail after the 32px scaled gap; narrow views stack. Search/category precede the roster. The existing shared viewport scale clamp remains active, including with a preferred 150% device scale.
fieldManual.focus: Selecting an entry focuses and reveals the detail heading; Back to search focuses search. Contextual hint/selection links focus the actual reference and align its heading at the reading viewport top, including narrow layouts with all 19 entries unfiltered. Native controls mirror semantic HTML values/focus and retain the gallery graphics fallback.
fieldManual.model: Actual installed GLB in an isolated orbit/zoom scene. Native controls occupy the left min(400px,45vw); at widths <=640px they occupy the top min(320px,45dvh). Existing blue Force token is the preview color; no color control. Loading status and fetch-failure alert/Retry reflect actual work. Escape cancels/disposes and restores initiating focus.
fieldManual.motion: Idle clips play only when neither the device setting nor operating-system reduced-motion preference requests reduction.
fieldManual.deferred: Training, owner playtesting and tuning recommendations remain separate work; this does not complete all first-playable guidance.
fieldManual.qualification: The nine reviewed desktop, narrow and preferred-150%-scale captures record browser presentation only; no screen-reader, Firefox, physical-touch or hardware qualification. Existing color detector advisories are not waived and do not establish a new palette.

contextualGuidance.world: Operate extension of Graphite Command Stations: existing graphite frames, ivory text, warm-metal actions and original line pictograms. No new palette, type, material, artwork or decorative motion.
contextualGuidance.profile: Versioned browser-local All/Important/Off preference, with Important the provisional default. Preference changes and Show hints again stage until Apply; Back discards the draft. Storage failure retains editable recovery.
contextualGuidance.hints: Low power, owned actor under attack, a visible enemy weapon with an authored damage multiplier above 100% against an owned actor's armour, and idle builder use permitted copied observations. The weapon bonus is not a universal counter or final-damage promise. Important excludes idle builder. Each appears once per local profile, with at least 20 simulation seconds between hints. Failed history persistence reports session-only retention.
contextualGuidance.presentation: One text-measured graphite hint frame below global feedback offers More and Dismiss. Optional HUD help labels active regions and hides the hint while enabled; selection/command labels require selection and notice labels require notices. Existing individual hover/focus tooltips retain action descriptions and live shortcuts. Empty selection leaves no station.
contextualGuidance.referenceNavigation: Hint More and supported selection Details links reuse the paused menu and same worker/world, update the selection target while paused, and focus/reveal the actual installed reference at the viewport top. Narrow galleries retain this alignment with all 19 entries unfiltered.
contextualGuidance.manual: 15 actor entries plus economy, fog, combat and current-binding guides. All entries, Units, Structures and Concepts and controls categories share the existing native gallery. Topic titles and text participate in search. Actor facts remain installed compiled content.
contextualGuidance.scope: Training, owner playtesting and tuning recommendations remain separate work; this records contextual guidance rather than completion of all first-playable guidance.
contextualGuidance.deferredDrift: The unrelated incumbent Audio paragraph and deviceAudio extension were deliberately preserved; their stale scope claims require a separate audio documentation refresh.

contentTools.world: Operate extension of Graphite Command Stations: original brick models lead; native square graphite controls, warm-metal actions, ivory focus and the existing shared Arial ramp/interface scale remain. No new palette, type tokens, assets or dependencies.
contentTools.entry: /tools/content and Home developer footer. Search names and IDs among 137 installed model definitions. The model query accepts only an installed qualified ID or exact registered model URL; unknown links show recovery without fetching arbitrary URLs.
contentTools.input: Open local GLB and model-canvas drop accept self-contained files up to 16 MiB. These inspection inputs never write content or upload files. Successful local loading clears the installed selection; local validation kind is editable while installed kinds and authored requirements stay fixed. Definition authoring opens owner-selected pack folders; multiple opened packs supply dependencies.
contentTools.layout: Desktop model left, full-height controls right at min(460px,42vw). At viewport width <=760px the model occupies the top 42dvh and controls the remaining 58dvh. Existing shared-panel interface scale applies. Back/title, status/errors and pinned Open/Retry stay outside the scrolling body. Definition authoring inherits this layout with pinned Open/Save, scrolling tabs/fields and compact name/pack/unsaved status. Conflict review replaces fields with comparison rows and pinned Reload/Keep choices. Sibling creation replaces the form with two framed name fields and pinned Create definition, Download changes ZIP and Cancel creation actions; the original model and source identity remain visible.
contentTools.presentation: Team choices exercise actual standard material slots. Rest is initial; explicit animation choices play authored clips. Auto LOD uses the provisional 96-metre threshold, with forced choices only for supported disjoint branches. Damage preview enables state_damaged below 66% and also state_critical below 33%, preserving independent LOD masks. These controls do not edit simulation state.
contentTools.validation: The CLI and viewer share modelRequirements and validateModel. Installed definitions supply actual requirements; local GLBs use common requirements for the chosen kind. Structurally renderable models remain inspectable with project errors/warnings. This is not complete pack/reference or external glTF conformance validation.
contentTools.inventories: Project diagnostics, materials, nodes and sockets use native expandable tables and the existing keyboard scroll bridge. Counts remain complete; lists disclose the 100-entry display cap.
contentTools.help: Open and validation-kind controls use contextual native hover/focus descriptions with semantic accessible descriptions. Definition fields expose schema descriptions and human units contextually; the picker exposes the full source path. Shared native focus help waits for measured bounds after scroll and chooses above a field when needed to clear the pinned footer. The focusable model canvas names orbit, zoom and local-file drop. Existing interface scale and semantic controls/usable graphics fallback remain.
contentTools.recovery: A failed candidate retains the last good model, controls and diagnostics, with pinned Retry repeating the failed source. Replacement/exit aborts pending fetches and disposes stale loads. Existing Field Manual/debug preview consumers remain supported.

definitionAuthoring.scope: 2-38b1 edits existing unit, structure and prop definitions from explicitly selected pack folders. Installed built-in definitions and simulation state remain intact; no uploads, new files, manifest mutations or binary edits.
definitionAuthoring.fields: Shared schemas derive scalar, enum, boolean, nested object, record and array fields; opaque values retain JSON input. Only applicable General/Combat/Visuals/Production/Upgrades/Eras tabs appear. Unassigned future properties appear in General. One field-change menu collects optional and collection changes; parsing errors block structural changes.
definitionAuthoring.writes: File System Access handles write only the selected existing file. The read-only folder-input fallback downloads a copy and keeps the source dirty. Writable folders are re-read for validation; only the candidate target JSON is substituted, allowing an explicitly reviewed corrupt target to be repaired. Failed writes abort their stream and retain the draft.
definitionAuthoring.checks: Before save/download, copied drafts pass shared schemas, pack resolution, reference/identity checks, gameplay compilation and model requirements. Errors prevent saving. Input/model files are not mutated during validation. These checks do not claim full asset/provenance/audio/glTF conformance or exact project formatter parity.
definitionAuthoring.reads: File snapshots, JSON, layers and runtime bytes use batches of 32 after applicable path/size preflight, retaining input order. Batching preserves the same resource limits, resolver, compiler, model checks and write gate.
definitionAuthoring.recovery: Loading, validation and saving lock fields and competing actions. Invalid numeric/JSON text survives tab changes; failed selection restores actual picker identity. Back/replacement retain save-or-discard guards and page unload retains the browser guard.
definitionAuthoring.conflicts: Latest target text is compared with the baseline before validation and immediately before the write stream. Changed text requires explicit Reload or Keep. Conflict review replaces editable fields with changed-leaf disk/draft comparisons; the disclosed display caps are 100 rows and 512 characters per value, with both underlying versions intact. Optimistic checks cannot prevent another program writing between the final comparison and stream close.
definitionAuthoring.bounds: Provisional limits: 2 MiB per JSON, 256 MiB combined runtime data, 10,000 directory entries and 32 directory levels. Source assets are listed but not read into validation memory.
definitionAuthoring.format: Current save/download output uses two-space JSON and a final newline; exact Biome formatting remains 2-38b2.

definitionCreation.scope: 2-38b3 creates a sibling from a clean selected unit, structure or prop. Authors enter a new display name and folder name. Kind and namespace stay intact; exact self-references are remapped. The complete co-located folder is copied with its models, editable sources, asset metadata and credits preserved. Built-in roster and simulation state remain intact.
definitionCreation.presentation: Code-led Operate extension of Graphite Command Stations. Original brick model left/above, two framed fields right/below, with pinned Create definition, Download changes ZIP and Cancel creation. Read-only folders omit Create definition. Shared graphite, ivory, warm-metal, Arial and interface-scale tokens remain unchanged; no new assets or decorative motion.
definitionCreation.writes: Shared checks gate both outputs. Writable folders are re-read and the selected template baseline is checked. Payload files are written, read back and validated before the updated manifest is published last. Destination and manifest conflicts stop creation. Existing files are never intentionally replaced. Browser file access remains optimistic rather than an atomic multi-file transaction.
definitionCreation.download: The stored ZIP contains the new folder and updated manifest. It is a changes bundle to extract into a copy of the selected pack, not a standalone pack. Read-only folders use this fallback; writable folders also offer it. Download never changes the source.
definitionCreation.recovery: Busy work locks controls. Errors retain entered names. Failed writes remove only new files still matching the operation and its uncommitted empty files; changed or inaccessible files are retained with recovery feedback. An uncertain or changed manifest preserves new files. Empty folders may remain for retry. Successful creation selects and previews the new definition; Cancel creation returns to the original definition.
definitionCreation.bounds: Template copies including editable sources are limited to 256 MiB; archive paths, entry count and total size are bounded. Existing combined-runtime and JSON bounds remain. Output retains two-space JSON and a final newline.

draftPlaytest.scope: 2-38c1 validates an unsaved existing definition and its checked original models for movement, health and placement in the existing debug worker. Normal combat/economy integration and its completed 2-38c2 scenario presets are recorded separately below.
draftPlaytest.presentation: Playtest draft reuses the native action beside Save. The retained HTML debug pane scrolls within bounded viewport space over real terrain, with Return to draft first and the explicit scope notice next. Existing Graphite editor tokens, assets and components remain unchanged; debug HTML styling does not become a new native design system.
draftPlaytest.snapshot: Writable packs are refreshed and only copied validation inputs receive the selected draft. Shared resolution, gameplay compilation, provenance and GLB checks gate launch. Checked model bytes become device-local Blob URLs; pack-qualified IDs and the existing human-to-sim conversion remain. No source/manifest writes, saved-definition changes, normal-match changes or simulation behavior/version change occur.
draftPlaytest.setup: The draft is preselected in the spawn palette. Node structures use Sandbox: Resources; naval units and authored shore/water footprints use Sandbox: Water; other definitions use Sandbox: Flat. Existing map, Force, palette and inspector controls stay manual. Two blue/red Force slots retain the existing faction identity; no opponent AI is implied.
draftPlaytest.recovery: The editor retains unsaved fields while its model/panel rendering is suspended. Return to draft remains available after worker failure, disposes worker/scene and temporary URLs, restores the native pane, resumes the model and returns focus to the initiating Playtest draft action. Leaving content tools also releases playtest resources.
draftPlaytest.reproduction: Canonical command-log export contains the actual copied simulation definitions and commands. Copy initial setup link is disabled because a URL cannot carry unsaved definitions or models. Export reproduces simulation, not an asset pack.

contentTools.deferred: The whole 2-38b task remains open: 2-38b2 retains full runtime audio, source freshness and exact project formatter parity. Scenario presets complete the remaining 2-38c2 slice. Asset editing/gizmos remain 2-38d, including socket/part gizmos, GLB export and damage-socket smoke/fire previews. Grid/scale reference, material mappings, native debug conversion and remaining documented editor controls remain follow-up work.
contentTools.qualification: No blanket phase acceptance, physical directory-picker/file-dragging, touch/IME, screen-reader, Firefox or hardware-performance qualification. No simulation version or gameplay outcome change.
contentTools.deferredDrift: Unrelated incumbent Audio wording and deviceAudio metadata remain preserved for a separate documentation refresh.

draftNormalSkirmish.scope: Bounded 2-38c2 normal combat/economy integration uses the actual normal-session worker with any of six installed authored maps. Basic bot and idle faction-opening presets keep the Eastern Collective mirror. Draft mirror adds one supported ground unit per Force to the normal starting kit, incrementing an existing entry where applicable, with an idle opponent controller and ordinary automatic combat. Structures use faction openings; aircraft/naval mirrors remain outside scope. Dry maps omit starting harvesters; harvester mirrors require ore. Normal starter-kit/map checks, combat, construction, production, resources and fog retain normal validation, commands and permissions without debug spawning.
draftNormalSkirmish.supported: Existing core first-playable definitions, compatible prerequisite-free priced units trained by their producers, and prerequisite-free priced Eastern Collective or neutral structures. Compatible cloned units enter only the temporary roster. Other packs, factions, props and definitions outside this compatibility gate retain debug checks; a rejected normal draft keeps edits and reports its restriction. Launch does not guarantee every edited recipe or movement domain can execute; normal engine validation still rejects incompatible commands. Normal starter-kit/map checks still gate launch.
draftNormalSkirmish.presentation: Code-led Operate extension of Graphite Command Stations: Skirmish draft beside Playtest draft/Save first opens a content-sized graphite modal with framed map/opponent/spawn/seed fields and pinned Cancel/Start actions, then existing native loading, match HUD and menu. Narrow modal content scrolls while actions remain available. Objective/clock/global controls stay above, economy and selection at lower left and circular minimap at right, retaining existing narrow stacking. Installed Field Manual labels the installed reference; actual actor stats, recipes and help read the draft catalog. No new composition, tokens, assets or components.
draftNormalSkirmish.snapshot: Shared checks gate copied inputs. The copied frozen scenario, metadata and checked model, wreck, icon and sound bytes stay fixed for the preview and every restart; later source-file edits do not replace the snapshot. Frozen sound bytes do not claim full 2-38b2 audio-validation parity.
draftNormalSkirmish.recovery: Loading Cancel or Return to draft restores retained edits, native panel/model rendering and focus to the initiating Skirmish draft action. Initialization/worker failure returns with a readable error. Each preview owns its worker, renderer and audio mixer; restarts reuse the mixer and snapshot. Return/failure disposes preview resources, decoded audio buffers and temporary asset URLs.
draftNormalSkirmish.persistence: No source/manifest writes, normal save slots, autosaves, replay storage or contextual guidance writes. Save/Load and quicksave are unavailable. Ordinary installed matches retain their existing persistence path. Normal quick play and saved setup defaults retain the installed Training Grounds mirror.
draftNormalSkirmish.qualification: Focused Chrome and WebKit journeys cover native scenario configuration, cancellation, actual map/kit/seed delivery, restart and retained edits. Desktop/narrow captures record the incumbent modal world. No whole phase/editor acceptance or human match-length/balance claim; physical touch/IME, screen readers, Firefox and hardware FPS remain unqualified.
draftNormalSkirmish.scenarioValidation: Named semantic fields own keyboard editing and mirror native focus. HTML owns modal focus and Escape; Map receives initial focus. Duplicate spawn sides or seeds outside unsigned 32-bit integer syntax/range expose an alert and disable Start. Cancel, Escape or leaving tools removes the panel without losing edits or starting a worker. Confirmed settings pass the existing draft/content and normal-worker validators.

modelActions.scope: Isolated firing/destruction portion of 2-38c2; native Fire, Destroy and Restore model remain visible while editing. Actions use the selected/Preview model snapshot; editing a field alone does not apply unsaved data. No source, save, normal-match or simulation-state changes.
modelActions.presentation: Code-led Operate extension of Graphite Command Stations: original model left and native pane right on desktop, stacked when narrow. Existing framed actions and contextual hover/focus descriptions explain effects and limits. No new palette, type, raster, composition or decorative motion; only requested functional effects.
modelActions.fire: Raw weapon-assigned sockets and suffixed nodes, or standalone muzzle sockets, supply actual world-space +Z direction. Available fire_recoil/attack accompanies a short original-code flash and fixed model-relative tracer. No audio, gameplay range, accuracy, burst or projectile simulation.
modelActions.destruction: Full authored death clip, otherwise at most 32 visible original geometry pieces using actual materials, then the paired authored wreck. Matching driven turret/barrel aiming carries relative to rest, preserving wreck tilt and non-part geometry. Unpaired standalone art disappears after its effect.
modelActions.restore: Clear effects and return the live model to rest with team, LOD and damage-state choices retained.
modelActions.recovery: Both bounded self-contained model inspections gate replacement. Live model and paired wreck stage and replace together; failed or superseded pairs retain the last good view with Retry. Replacement/disposal releases owned effect meshes, materials and model containers. Draft playtests pause the retained effect clock. Shared no-options preview callers remain compatible.
modelActions.qualification: Implementation evidence is limited to the current Chrome/WebKit browser scope; it does not qualify Firefox, physical touch/IME, screen readers or hardware FPS.

worldWaypoints.world: Local Operate extension of Graphite Command Stations: existing cyan routes, original terrain/models and native contextual HUD. No new palette, font, asset, panel or ornamental motion.
worldWaypoints.presentation: Only selected controlled actors' published pending markers participate. Hover adds a small diamond; terrain-aligned route previews update during dragging. Picking uses CSS pixels across graphics scaling. Spatial move/attack-move destinations use cell centres; build destinations use grid origins. Target-based items use only already-permitted copied positions and support removal rather than spatial dragging.
worldWaypoints.commands: Release invokes the same HUD unit.editQueued path; right-click invokes unit.cancelQueued. Existing grants, worker validation and feedback remain authoritative. Shared build-group rows follow accepted edits/removals, with no payment before execution. Current orders and selection remain intact.
worldWaypoints.recovery: Escape, blur, lost pending marker/selection, pointer cancellation and invalid or HUD drops cancel the preview. Right-drag retains camera panning. Empty selection leaves no station or dock hit area.
worldWaypoints.help: Existing queue buttons retain keyboard editing/removal. Localized button-title help maps into native Babylon hover/focus tooltips; no browser HTML title is added to the world canvas.

qualification.review: Independent five-section finish review found no material fix; seven actual interaction captures were valid.
qualification.browserProof: Real-worker world-marker drag/remove journey passed Chromium and WebKit, 2/2; raw log /tmp/neo-world-waypoint-aim-browsers.log.
qualification.technicalProof: Independent renderer checks passed 3/3 with 23 assertions; controller probe passed.
qualification.detector: Four pre-existing static findings remain in /tmp/neo-world-waypoint-detector.json: hidden portrait placeholder and three color advisories. The detector is limited evidence, not a visual verdict or new token authority.
qualification.limits: No physical touch, physical IME, screen-reader, Firefox, hardware FPS or blanket phase acceptance. Patrol and factory-route gameplay remain outside this extension.

worldWaypoints.deferredDrift: Unrelated stale Audio scope wording and deviceAudio metadata remain preserved for a separate documentation refresh.

replayCameras.world: Scoped Graphite Command Stations extension: original camera pictogram in the compact vision/exit group, existing warm selected well while following, ivory synchronized focus and contextual help. No new identity, tokens, raster, quality board or replacement composition.
replayCameras.interaction: Native activation and C cycle Free camera and available recorded-seat choices; the semantic select retains keyboard ownership and mirrors focus. Vision remains independent. Keyboard/edge/drag pan, rotation, wheel zoom, minimap navigation and combat-event pans return to free camera. Seeking restores the selected recorded pose; before its first tick, playback returns to free. Camera-free files retain a dimmed control with contextual explanation.
replayCameras.recording: Actual local-human target, rotation, pitch and distance are captured against observed simulation ticks, replacing the latest pose for paused edits. Initial capture precedes unpause; terminal pose freezes before result-screen navigation. Loaded matches record only from the resumed tick. Bots receive no invented cameras; draft playtests do not record. Playback binary-searches and interpolates poses with shortest-angle wrap, holds while paused and uses the current viewport aspect ratio.
replayCameras.metadata: Optional cameras are accepted in both replay envelope formats. Actual normal result downloads retain format-1 worker records and camera metadata; verified library exports upgrade to portable format-2 frames/map identity while preserving cameras through rename, export and import. Strict fields, finite bounded poses, unique recorded seats, monotonic ticks within duration and an aggregate 144001-sample limit apply before storage/watch; existing two-hour and 64 MiB file limits remain.
replayCameras.boundary: Camera annotations are untrusted presentation metadata and are not authenticated by simulation-history verification. They never enter commands, canonical state, keyframes or hashes; simulation outcomes and version remain unchanged. Camera-free portable and raw legacy records retain free playback.

qualification.browser: Four corrected real-browser replay/paid-production journeys passed in /tmp/neo-camera-browser-confirm.log: current stable Chrome 22.4s/17.4s and current Playwright WebKit 29.0s/22.3s. They cover native pointer/C/select follow, rewind, manual pan override, rotated/zoomed data, portable import/export and camera-free legacy playback. The actual normal format-1 download was inspected. Earlier four failures exposed dropped metadata and are superseded.
qualification.review: Fresh scoped finish review independently opened all eight valid captures and returned SHIP without a material correction. Full repository fix/typecheck/test/build passed. Final focused parser checks passed seven tests/60 assertions; independent technical checks passed seven probes/60 assertions.
qualification.limits: Loaded-match segments and post-result pose freezing were source-reviewed, not independently browser exercised. Maximum-size replay stress, hardware FPS, physical touch/IME and screen-reader user testing remain unqualified. Delayed live spectating and full replay/spectator phase acceptance remain open.
qualification.detector: Ran once at /tmp/neo-camera-design-detect.json; existing #efa394 advisory remains advisory. No rerun or palette expansion.

components.name: Native command icon
components.description: HTML preview of the Babylon icon command: warm hover frame, ivory focus frame, primary armed well and inspectable unavailable state. Production command positions stay fixed while shortcut captions follow the applied device profile; Q is the Grid default shown in this static preview.

components.name: Native selection station

components.name: Shared native panel
components.description: Static HTML preview of the shared native Settings/pause/loading/Load/results vocabulary at base scale. Production uses measured Babylon layout, original SVG disclosure marks and synchronized semantic controls; this preview does not implement persistence or the canvas renderer. Loading mirrors semantic stage value/max into a warm-metal progress fill and retains Cancel; failure retains the actual alert, Retry and Back. Replay library and verification/failure dialogs reuse this renderer; replay verification mirrors actual terminal progress and failure returns to Replays without deleting its record. Save-before-leave/restart/load and browser Back reuse its separate modal with a fixed-header Cancel, primary Save and explicit discard. Pending work disables competing actions; failed saves preserve the world and edited name for retry. Cancel restores prior pause/focus; ending/disposal suppresses late continuations. Field Manual reuses its search/category controls, rich tables and expandable detail controls; the isolated model inspector reuses its native status, failure and Retry vocabulary. Device camera preferences reuse the framed percentage choice and square checkbox, permanent semantic descriptions and synchronized focus. Mouse sensitivity controls wheel zoom and right/middle drag separately from keyboard/edge speed and programmatic zoom; inversion reverses only horizontal middle-drag rotation. Apply saves, Back/cancel restores saved preferences, and failed Apply restores the saved preview while keeping fields editable for retry. Version-one choices migrate intact with 100% sensitivity and inversion off.

narrative.overview:
The normal match uses thin steel frames, warm metal command pictograms and original model portraits around a dominant battlefield. Economy stacks beside the native selection station, which integrates Force identity, type counts, contextual icon commands, build/train recipes and queue progress. A circular minimap anchors the right. Compact objective, clock/speed and global controls occupy separate top regions. Quiet controls support reading resources, inspecting real actor state and issuing orders; an empty selection leaves no station. There is no decorative animation; minimap activity and original work poses communicate actual game state. Brass silhouettes identify hover and the selected truck's current visible ore target.

Home shares graphite steel, warm metal and original assets through native Babylon GUI. An original angular vector wordmark introduces an authored Dragon Tank on an octagonal plinth. Plain, framed actions sit beside the model on desktop and below it in portrait. Slow display rotation stops when reduced motion is requested.

Skirmish setup extends the native graphite field with compact Force rows, framed inputs and a top-down preview of authored Training Grounds. Content scrolls within a fixed header and action area; validation feedback stays above the actions.

Settings, pause actions, Objectives, Current controls and named saves extend the same native graphite vocabulary through a shared content-sized panel. In a match it floats above the dimmed battlefield; the HTML dialog owns modal focus and Escape while its separate canvas leaves the world renderer intact. Save-before-leave, restart and load decisions use that same panel vocabulary in a separate modal, preserving the parent pane and original thumbnail source.

Device camera preferences extend Settings with the existing framed percentage choice and square checkbox: Mouse camera sensitivity and Invert drag rotation. Permanent help distinguishes mouse behavior from keyboard/edge pan speed. Preview, Apply and Back preserve the shared saved-state safety interaction.

The device-local Keyboard controls editor extends that shared native panel with category, action and primary/alternate choices, staged key capture and explicit conflict feedback. Applied bindings update the running match's captions while command positions stay fixed; graphite controls and warm status/coral alerts reuse the existing panel vocabulary.

The Audio pane extends those same Settings from Home and a match with channel and integer-percentage choices, live preview, Test sound and explicit Apply or Back. Graphite fields, warm-metal actions and coral recovery retain the incumbent world. Audio descriptions appear on native hover/focus and in semantic accessible descriptions; status and recovery remain visible.

Load and results extend that shared native panel with original match thumbnails, selected-slot details, framed tabs, history plots and complete scrollable tables. Their existing controllers and semantic HTML remain authoritative; the canvas copies display values and invokes the same actions.

Loading and failure use the same content-sized graphite panel. Warm stage text and a warm-metal fill show actual initialization progress; a framed Cancel action remains available. Failure shows the actual coral alert with primary Retry and ordinary Back actions. The loading dialog owns a separate native canvas so the initializing world cannot remove its feedback by redrawing the application root.

The local Replay library extends the gallery with the original installed Training Grounds preview and selected-record actions. Its viewer retains a dominant battlefield, warm-metal transport pictograms and timeline, permitted Force readouts and original active-production thumbnails, with the circular minimap at the right. Semantic controls own keyboard behavior and mirror focus into the native interface. Verified combat intervals and public Force outcomes extend the transport with a compact marker row and previous/next navigation, filtered by the current view. This records the first playable Eastern Collective local mirror, including verified portable frames and explicit map identity. Optional native statistics extend the viewer below player observations: Economy and Military plot permitted sampled history, Production shows original queued-unit thumbnails and real progress, and Orders leads with accepted-order APM. Existing graphite frames, compact Arial, warm-metal actions and semantic controls carry this extension. Recorded player cameras add a compact native camera pictogram beside vision, selected while following; C cycles follow/free modes and manual navigation returns to free mode. Delayed live spectating remains deferred. The timeline explicitly participates in sequential keyboard focus after speed and vision, retaining its native focus frame.

Field Manual extends the same gallery with original actor icons, searchable roster rows, four concept/control entries and compiled-statistic tables. Desktop gives the selected entry the larger reading column; narrow layouts stack. Contextual links focus and reveal the actual entry at the top of the reading viewport, preserving the paused match. An isolated original-model orbit view pairs the real GLB with native controls, using the existing graphite, ivory, warm-metal and blue Force tokens. Idle animation respects either reduced motion preference. The embedded pane preserves the paused battlefield.

Contextual guidance extends the native HUD and Settings without changing the visual world. Optional labels name active HUD regions; one brief hint drawn from permitted observations offers More and Dismiss below global feedback. Existing individual action descriptions remain on hover/focus. Guidance preferences and history reset stay staged until Apply in the shared native panel. Reference links reuse the paused menu and manual rather than adding a teaching overlay.

Content tools extend Graphite Command Stations with original models as the main subject and a native graphite inspection pane. Existing framed choices change actual team materials, authored clips, supported LOD branches and damage-state nodes. Expandable tables expose project checks and parsed model inventories. The model starts at rest; animation follows an explicit clip choice. Existing definition authoring extends this same pane with schema-derived fields, applicable tabs and one optional/collection-change menu. Compact source identity and unsaved status remain visible; contextual help carries descriptions, units and full paths. Conflict review temporarily replaces fields with changed-value rows and pinned Reload/Keep choices. A clean selected definition also supplies an authored template for a sibling: two framed name fields replace the editing form, with pinned Create definition, Download changes ZIP and Cancel creation actions. The original model and source identity remain visible. Playtest draft beside Save opens the retained HTML debug controls over real terrain, with Return to draft first in a bounded scrolling pane. The validated unsaved definition and checked local model snapshot support movement, health and placement. Skirmish draft beside it first opens a native graphite scenario modal with framed map, opponent, spawn and seed fields and pinned Cancel/Start actions, then the native loading panel and selected authored-map match. Its existing HUD exposes actual draft stats and recipes; Installed Field Manual identifies the installed reference. Return to draft restores the retained native editor and initiating action focus. Fire, Destroy and Restore model extend the retained pane with explicit isolated socket, recoil and destruction checks; unsaved fields apply only through Preview model. Functional model effects reuse original geometry without decorative motion. This records model inspection (2-38a), existing-definition authoring (2-38b1), sibling creation (2-38b3) and draft debug checks (2-38c1), plus bounded normal combat/economy integration (2-38c2). The six-map scenario presets complete the remaining 2-38c2 slice. Full runtime audio, source freshness and exact formatter parity remain 2-38b2. Asset editing remains open, including socket/part gizmos, GLB export and damage-socket smoke/fire previews.

Pending route editing extends the existing cyan battlefield overlay with a small hover diamond and a terrain-aligned drag preview. The native selection station retains its keyboard queue controls and localized hover/focus help. No new panel, palette, font or asset accompanies the gesture; empty selection leaves no station.

This records the built Home, Skirmish setup, shared native panels, loading, Load, results, local Replays, Field Manual, content-model inspection, definition authoring, sibling creation, draft debug checks and temporary normal skirmishes, and native normal match HUD. Debug retains HTML/CSS presentation; native surfaces retain synchronized semantic controls and usable HTML graphics fallbacks. The direction comes from the first body comment in `../../apps/web/index.html`; implementation evidence is `../render/src/scene/menu.ts`, `src/features/main-menu/index.ts`, `../render/src/scene/skirmish.ts`, `src/features/skirmish/index.ts`, `../render/src/scene/panel.ts`, `../render/src/scene/panel-content.ts`, `src/shared/native-panel.ts`, `src/shared/panel-content.ts`, `src/app/index.ts`, `src/features/settings/`, `src/features/in-game-menu/`, `../render/src/scene/battlefield-hud.ts`, `../render/src/scene/battlefield-map.ts`, `src/features/match/native-hud.ts` and `src/features/match/`, `src/features/load-game/`, `src/features/post-match/`, `src/features/replays/`, `../render/src/scene/replay-hud.ts`, `src/features/replays/analytics.ts`, `../render/src/scene/replay-chart.ts`, `../render/src/scene/replay-production.ts`, `src/features/field-manual/`, `src/features/onboarding/`, `src/features/settings/guidance-screen.ts` and `src/app/shell.css`. Field Manual's local direction is the emitted comment in `src/features/field-manual/index.ts`; it extends the incumbent world rather than defining a new one. Contextual guidance's emitted contract is in `src/features/onboarding/match.ts`; its Operate direction is recorded in `.impeccable/surfaces/src-features-onboarding-match-ts.md`. Content tools' local contract is in `src/features/content-editor/index.ts` and `.impeccable/surfaces/src-features-content-editor-index-ts.md`; its implementation also uses `src/features/content-editor/content-tools.css`, `model.ts`, `definition-editor.ts`, `definition-form.ts`, `definition-pack.ts`, `creation.ts`, `creation-write.ts`, `archive.ts`, `playtest.ts`, `skirmish-playtest.ts`, `scenario-panel.ts` and `scenarios.ts`, plus `src/features/debug/session.ts`, `catalog.ts`, `palette.ts` and `reproduction.ts`. Existing definition boundaries are recorded in `../../docs/project/decisions/2026-11-04-browser-definition-authoring.md`. Sibling creation is recorded in `../../docs/project/decisions/2026-11-04-definition-creation.md`. Draft debug checks are recorded in `../../docs/project/decisions/2026-11-04-draft-debug-playtest.md`. Temporary normal skirmishes are recorded in `../../docs/project/decisions/2026-11-04-draft-normal-skirmish.md`. Scenario configuration follows `../../docs/project/decisions/2026-11-04-draft-scenario-presets.md`. Isolated model actions use `../render/src/units/preview-actions.ts` and follow `../../docs/project/decisions/2026-11-04-model-action-previews.md`. Pending route editing follows the WAYPOINTS EXTENSION in `../../apps/web/index.html` and `.impeccable/surfaces/src-features-match-waypoints-ts.md`; its evidence is `src/features/match/waypoints.ts`, `src/features/match/session.ts`, `src/features/match/hud.ts`, `src/features/match/native-hud.ts` and `../render/src/units/waypoints.ts`.

Complete action descriptions on hover/focus and content-sized actor Details.
Native Home actions, original vector lettering and an authored model display.
Native setup fields, compact Force rows and an authored terrain preview.
Native content-sized Settings and pause panes over an intact match renderer.
Native device camera preferences with separate mouse sensitivity, drag inversion and saved-state recovery.
Native staged keyboard bindings with explicit conflicts and live match captions.
Native Audio preview and testing with contextual help and explicit save/cancel recovery.
Native save-before-replacement decisions with explicit cancellation and recovery.
Native save galleries with original match thumbnails and selected-slot details.

rules.name: The Battlefield Rule
rules.body: Keep persistent controls at the viewport edges and leave the central canvas available for play.

rules.name: The Complete Recipe Rule
rules.body: Keep complete prices, build times, requirements and unavailable reasons reachable through action hover/focus descriptions.

rules.name: The Actual Progress Rule
rules.body: Draw progress from the semantic value and maximum; keep stage status, cancellation and actual failure recovery available throughout initialization.

dos: Do preserve the owner's original model assets and authored names.
Do use real match state for portraits, counters, availability and feedback.
Do preserve full recipe values and readable unavailable explanations.
Do retain accessible action names, visible focus and contextual command switching.
Do keep native Home, setup, panel and match controls synchronized with semantic HTML and preserve the graphics fallback.
Do honor device and operating-system reduced motion in Home and Field Manual model displays.
Do use authored terrain, resource positions and selected spawns for the setup preview.
Do size shared panels from measured content and keep modal rendering separate from the match canvas.
Do preserve original save thumbnails, plot descriptions and every result-table row through responsive scrolling.
Do keep loading feedback independent of world redraws and retain real progress, cancellation and failure recovery in semantic HTML.
donts: Don't promote fallback HTML shell or debug styling into the recorded native surfaces or match HUD.
Don't substitute borrowed artwork or text glyphs for original model and SVG assets.
Don't add ornamental animation that competes with battlefield activity.
